stories.title: The treasury bond mess: is this the demise of the US as a safe haven?
stories.summary: The US is scooping up treasury bonds in an effort to raise their price and push yields down – but it’s not working The bond market is driving the Trump administration crazy. opening: The US is scooping up treasury bonds in an effort to raise their price and push yields down – but it’s not working.
The bond market is driving the Trump administration crazy.
body: Last week, the treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, announced that the government would sharply ramp up its purchase of treasury bonds, in an effort to raise their price and thus push down their yield, which amounts to the interest rate the government pays on its debt.
It didn’t quite work as planned.
Yields on treasurys fell after Bessent’s bond market intervention but soon bounced back.
By Friday afternoon, the yield on the 10-year treasury was back near where it was before the secretary’s announcement.

stories.title: Hainan expands 30-day visa-free policy to 61 countries
stories.summary: Residents of Vietnam and Kyrgyzstan became eligible on August 20, China’s National Immigration Administration said
article_sentences: According to a post on the agency’s WeChat account, residents of two more countries, Vietnam and Kyrgyzstan, became eligible for the policy on August 20.
Citizens of these countries in other parts of China outside Hainan are also eligible for 240-hour visa-free transit.

The agency noted that throughout their stay in China’s southernmost province, foreign nationals entering visa-free with ordinary passports may remain on the island for tourism, business, or private visits.
However, those wishing to visit Hainan for work, study, or journalistic activities must still obtain the appropriate authorization document in advance.

According to China’s immigration authorities, expanding the visa-free policy in Hainan is a "practical measure aimed at systematically increasing high-level openness." The policy is expected to promote "building a community with a shared future," fostering even closer ties between China and neighboring countries, enhancing mutual trust, and advancing international cooperation across a range of areas.
Simplifying entry procedures and conditions of stay in Hainan is expected to promote the development of trade, investment projects, as well as cultural and humanitarian programs.
The agency noted that as the province becomes more open, local authorities face the task of ensuring that cross-border passenger flows remain safe and orderly.

According to China’s National Immigration Administration, a well-balanced combination of measures to increase openness and maintain border controls "will more effectively promote high-quality development."
